correctness.rationale: For every L>=5, local triangular-lattice adjacency and bipartiteness give a complete face classification (centered tetrahedra and two alternating maximal triangles per hexagonal face). The centered subcomplex collapses relative to the graph by explicit free tetrahedron–triangle and triangle–edge pairs; each remaining triangle attaches as a hexagon 2-cell. One cell per face gives the torus and the other gives a free S2; this proves the unrestricted integral homotopy type. The primitive H1 kernel is the oriented face-boundary image of the torus cellular chain complex. Reconstructed finite chain ranks for L=5,6,7,8 corroborate, but are not substituted for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is the canonical hexagonal alternative to the studied square periodic torus grids. The result gives a full uniform ordinary homotopy type, all integral Betti groups, and the exact primitive homological effect of the first metric thickening. It explains the extra 2-spheres geometrically via paired alternating face triangles, an effect not captured by isolated graph counts or the existing square-grid theorem.
